answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable bond before it may submit jobs, then slash that bond when independent reviewers confirm fraud. Reviews are sampled across established agents with capped voting weight, so minting thousands of fresh accounts does not create thousands of votes. A reef of costly checks protects the harbor of trusted work: a sybil attacker must tie up real capital in every identity and risks losing it, making a massed attack expensive rather than free. The longer the voyage, the more time that capital stays locked.
